typed_core.name: issuer_name
typed_core.why: identity — who produced the evidence (bank, creditor, servicer)

typed_core.name: obligation_type
typed_core.why: disambiguator — what kind of obligation was paid

typed_core.name: account_or_case_number_masked
typed_core.why: PII — ties the payment to the obligation/account

typed_core.name: property_address_if_applicable
typed_core.why: identity — links to a property when relevant (flattened from address)

typed_core.name: payment_date
typed_core.why: identity — when the payment was made

typed_core.name: source_account_last4
typed_core.why: PII — ties the payment to the borrower's account
typed_core.prompt_hint: Exists to tie the payment to the borrower's own funds — capture last-4 verbatim, never infer full digits

typed_core.name: cleared_or_completed_indicator
typed_core.why: processor — did the payment actually clear

typed_core.name: paid_in_full_indicator
typed_core.why: processor — debt fully paid -> excludable from DTI

typed_core.name: billing_or_due_period
typed_core.why: processor — which period this payment covers

typed_core.name: loan_number
typed_core.why: identity — links to the loan file

nested_lists.name: recurring_payment_history
nested_lists.shape_reason: when the document is a payment history rather than a single receipt, each period is a row; can be many rows, so flat + one source keeps it under the 16,384 ceiling

fields.name: source
fields.why: provenance snippet for the payment row

rejected.name: signature_blocks, notary_block
rejected.reason: a payment receipt is not executed/notarized

rejected.name: creditor_receipt_or_confirmation
rejected.reason: free-form object; presence covered by cleared/paid-in-full -> catch-all

encoding_variations: 'Payment date' vs 'posted/cleared date' can differ by days — keep both; DTI/sourcing cares about cleared funds

Paid-off status appears as a 'paid in full' stamp, a '$0.00 balance' line, or an 'account closed' status — keep paid_in_full_indicator, balance_after_payment, and account_status_after_payment so a bare stamp is corroborated
Obligation type may be prose ('auto loan', 'collection', 'credit card') — keep verbatim; it drives whether the payoff helps qualification

open_questions.q: Single receipt vs payment history. The document may be one payment or a ledger.
options: populate recurring_payment_history only when a ledger is present, else leave []
open_questions.recommendation: keep the one flat nested list; flag that most instances leave it empty

open_questions.q: Which cleared signal is authoritative? cleared_or_completed_indicator, paid_in_full_indicator, and account_status_after_payment overlap.
open_questions.recommendation: keep all three (they corroborate); let a future DTI-exclusion rule pick the trusted one

open_questions.q: check_reference_or_trace_number PII class. Restricted but not last-4-masked.
options: keep as a plain restricted typed field
open_questions.recommendation: keep typed, flag GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): mask account-like identifiers (policy/account/plan numbers, wire/ACH trace, check references) via _PII_FIELDS; leave addresses and public-record case numbers PLAIN; DOB is unmasked (pii null).

notes: No rules consume this type today, so there is no rule floor; every field earns its place on identity, PII, processor use, or disambiguation.
account_or_case_number_masked and source_account_last4 both need _PII_FIELDS registration (pre_masked true).
check_reference_or_trace_number is a restricted trace identifier kept as a typed field and flagged for possible PII registration; its reason_class is processor (not registered as PII in this draft).
Prompt hint (doc-level): this proves a payment/payoff — the load-bearing outputs are the amount, the cleared status, and the resulting balance / paid-in-full flag.
Prompt hint (doc-level): distinguish a single payment receipt from a payment history (the latter fills the nested list).
